facts.fact_text: The youth group Committee for Protection of Rights of Young Political Prisoners (Gənc Siyasi Məhbusların Hüquqlarını Müdafiə Komitəsi) decided to hold a demonstration at around 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011 at the Seaside Boulevard in Baku.
The applicants attended the demonstration on 22 May 2011 at the Seaside Boulevard in Baku.
According to the applicants, the demonstration on 22 May 2011 was intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstration on 22 May 2011 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants of the demonstration on 22 May 2011 were a group of ten to twelve persons.
Shortly after the demonstration on 22 May 2011 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
According to the applicants, as soon as they noticed the police approaching they attempted to run away and leave the place of the demonstration.
According to the applicants, police officers followed and caught the applicants after they attempted to run away from the demonstration.
All three applicants were arrested by police officers V.I. and R.G. at around 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011.

Police officers V.I. and R.G. submitted a report (raport) to a superior police officer stating that at around 5.30 p.m. at the Seaside Boulevard a group of young persons attempted to hold an unauthorised demonstration by shouting out loud and disturbed people.
Police officers V.I. and R.G. stated in their report that when they wanted to calm down those persons, the persons ignored them.
Police officers V.I. and R.G. stated in their report that they brought the persons to police station No. 39.
Between 6.15 p.m. and 6.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011, administrative-offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued by police officer T.R. in respect of all three applicants.

The administrative-offence reports stated that at 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011, by deliberately failing to comply with the lawful order of the police, the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 310 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
All three applicants refused to sign the respective administrative-offence reports.
The administrative-offence reports contained pre-printed texts declaring that the arrested person was familiarised with the report.

The administrative-offence reports contained pre-printed texts declaring that the rights and obligations under Articles 371, 372, 374, 377, 379 and 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Republic of Azerbaijan were explained to the arrested person.
Subsequently, police officer T.R. prepared administrative-arrest reports (inzibati qaydada tutma haqqında protokol) with respect to the first and second applicants.

According to the administrative-arrest reports, copies of which were submitted to the Court by the Government, the first applicant had been subjected to administrative arrest at 7 p.m. on 22 May 2011.

According to the administrative-arrest reports, copies of which were submitted to the Court by the Government, the second applicant had been subjected to administrative arrest at 7 p.m. on 22 May 2011.
The administrative-arrest reports stated that the first applicant had been released on 22 May 2011, without specifying the time of the alleged release.
The administrative-arrest reports stated that the second applicant had been released on 22 May 2011, without specifying the time of the alleged release.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after the arrest or while they were kept in police custody.

Article 49 of the 1995 Constitution of Azerbaijan provides that everyone has the right, having notified respective governmental bodies in advance, to assemble with other people peacefully and without arms, to organise meetings, demonstrations, protests and marches, and to stage pickets.

Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, advance written notification is required in order to agree upon the place and time of an assembly and upon the route of a march, with the purpose of enabling the relevant local executive authority to take necessary measures.
Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, the notification has to be done in writing five days before the demonstration.
Under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.
Article 8 §§ IV and V of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with powers to prohibit a public assembly.
Article 8 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with powers to stop a public assembly.

Article 9 §§ II and VII of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with powers to restrict or change the place, route and/or time of a public assembly.
Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with powers to designate specific areas for public assemblies.

At the material time, Article 14 § I(2) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power, when necessary, to stop an assembly which has not been notified to the authorities beforehand, save for spontaneous assemblies.

At the material time, Article 14 § I(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to apprehend and remove from the place where an event is being held persons who came carrying weapons, rocks, pieces of wood and glass, clubs that may pose a threat to people's life and safety or damage property, explosives, flammables, or radioactive materials.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(2) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to order the organisers and participants of an assembly to use all available opportunities to stop the assembly and to disperse, in execution of orders specified under Article 8 paragraphs V and VI of that Law.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(3) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to warn organisers and participants that physical force or exceptional measures will be used against them if the order to stop the assembly and to disperse is not complied with.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to use physical force or exceptional measures in order to stop an assembly and disperse participants, in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

At the material time, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that any breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen Azerbaijani manats.

At the material time, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with the lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five Azerbaijani manats or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.

At the material time, Article 376.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that if it is impossible for the lawyer chosen by the person against whom administrative-offence proceedings are being carried out to attend, a judge shall appoint a lawyer for that person in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

At the material time, Article 376.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that if a person subjected to an administrative arrest has no possibility to hire a lawyer due to his or her financial situation, his or her legal assistance shall be funded by the State, and in this case a lawyer may not refuse to carry out his or her duties.

At the material time, Article 396.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an authorised official may use measures including administrative arrest in order to prevent administrative offences, to establish the identity of a person, to draw up an administrative-offence report if this cannot be done at the place of the administrative offence and if the drawing up of a report is important, to ensure the correct and timely examination of administrative-offence cases, and to ensure the implementation of decisions in administrative-offence cases.

At the material time, Article 398.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that administrative arrest, that is the short-term restriction of an individual's liberty, may be applied in exceptional circumstances when deemed necessary for ensuring the correct and timely examination of an administrative-offence case or for the implementation of a decision in an administrative-offence case, except for instances set out in legislation.

At the material time, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity shall be given an opportunity to familiarise with the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity has the right to a copy of the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 414.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that a report concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be sent to a judge for examination immediately after it has been drawn up.

At the material time, Article 422.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that cases concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be examined on the day of receipt by the court of an administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 422.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that cases against persons subjected to administrative arrest shall be examined at the latest within 48 hours of their arrest.
Chapter 28 of the Code of Administrative Offences enumerates the participants of administrative proceedings and their rights and obligations.

Chapter 28 of the Code of Administrative Offences does not mention the prosecution — a police officer, public prosecutor or any other public official representing the prosecution — as a participant of the proceedings.

The administrative-arrest reports stated that the first applicant had been released on 22 May 2011, without specifying the time of the alleged release.
The administrative-arrest reports stated that the second applicant had been released on 22 May 2011, without specifying the time of the alleged release.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after the arrest or while they were kept in police custody.
On 23 May 2011, the day after his arrest, the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, was brought before the Sabail District Court.
According to the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, the hearing before the Sabail District Court began at 12.40 p.m. and was very brief.

According to the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, members of the public, including human rights defenders and journalists, were not allowed to attend the hearing before the Sabail District Court.
According to the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, the Sabail District Court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearing to the public.
The first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, was not represented by any lawyer at the hearing before the Sabail District Court.
According to the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, he was not given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice.
The first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, stated before the Sabail District Court that he was not guilty of disobeying a lawful order of a police officer.
The only witness questioned during the court hearing of the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, before the Sabail District Court was police officer R.G.

Police officer R.G. testified at the hearing of the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, that at around 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011 a group of persons attempted to hold an unauthorised demonstration by shouting out loud and disturbed people.
Police officer R.G. testified that when he and his colleague wanted to calm down those persons, among them the first applicant Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, they disobeyed a lawful police order.
Police officer R.G. testified that he and his colleague brought the persons to police station No. 39 where administrative-offence reports were issued in their respect.
The Sabail District Court found that the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, had failed to stop participating in the unauthorised demonstration.
The Sabail District Court convicted the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Sabail District Court sentenced the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, to seven days' administrative detention.

The first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, lodged an appeal before the Baku Court of Appeal arguing that his conviction was in violation of his rights because the demonstration in which he had participated had been peaceful.
The first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, complained in his appeal before the Baku Court of Appeal that his arrest had been unlawful.
The first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, complained in his appeal before the Baku Court of Appeal that the hearing before the Sabail District Court had not been fair.
The first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, requested the Baku Court of Appeal to quash the Sabail District Court's decision.
The first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, was represented before the Baku Court of Appeal by a lawyer of his own choice.
On 31 May 2011 the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the first applicant Mr Agasif Ibrahimov's appeal.
On 31 May 2011 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the decision of the Sabail District Court in the case of the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, stating that its findings had been correct.

The Baku Court of Appeal noted that at the Sabail District Court hearing the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, had refused the assistance of a State-funded lawyer and had decided to defend himself in person.

The Sabail District Court found that the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, had failed to stop participating in the unauthorised demonstration.
The Sabail District Court convicted the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Sabail District Court sentenced the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, to eight days' administrative detention.
